DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2014_family.do infixes DA3032 at the ES3032 DATA LIST positions (P1801..P1805 = cols 146-150, identical to ES3032 line 13 and to the questionnaire's column codes (146)-(150)) under lower-cased names, and Bookmark 9 sets item = the variable name (p1801..p1805; lower-casing is Stata naming) -- nothing positional, so Step 5b is exempt and no verification_/verify_ files were written. LABELS vs QUESTIONNAIRE: ES3032 VARIABLE LABELS P1801-P1805 were compared with the P.18 rows of cues3032.pdf read from a 300-dpi render of scanned page 4 (not OCR), dot leaders dropped and the wrapped rows ('...que no / puede tener hijos/as', '...a través de un / vientre de alquiler') rejoined: 5/5 agree character for character (asserted in build.R), so item_text is both the label and the questionnaire row, with no override. VALUE LABELS identical on all 5: 1 'Más bien a favor' 2 'Más bien en contra' 3 '(NO LEER) Depende de los casos' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.' -- matching the questionnaire's printed list. RESP BY DESIGN: the .do recodes 3 (the volunteered, not-read-out 'depends on the case'), 8 and 9 to missing, so live resp is {1,2} and option rows ship for those two codes only. Dropped by the .do, per item p1801..p1805: code 3 = 92/223/287/302/468 (1372 total); code 8 = 45/115/76/155/115 (506); code 9 = 8/19/10/15/9 (61). DA3032 carries no code 0 and no blanks on cols 146-150, so P.18 was asked of all 2464 respondents (no filter printed above it); 78 respondents gave 3/8/9 on all five items and have no rows, which is why live has 2386 ids. CHECKED, decisive: reading DA3032 (2464 records, all 385 bytes; id = row number) at cols 146-150, dropping 3/8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 254 and cov_age cols 255-256 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 10381 rows both, 2386 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 resp, 0 cov_sex and 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as the Stata value label (Hombre 5092 rows, Mujer 5289). Live item x resp (1/2): p1801 2242/77, p1802 1415/692, p1803 1798/293, p1804 1241/751, p1805 816/1056 -- every item uses both levels; per-item n 2319/2107/2091/1992/1872. Coherence: the infertile heterosexual couple is near-unanimously favoured (96.7%) and the woman over 50 is the only case with a majority against (56.4%), as the content predicts. validate_items.R --table-sets passed (5 items, resp {1,2}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): instructions = the full P.18 question text verbatim from cues3032.pdf, including the lower-case 'ud.' and the trailing '...?' as printed, shared by all five rows, so instructions not section_prompt, one trivial section; the '(NO LEER)' marker belongs to the dropped option 3 and is not shipped. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3032 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by this project ('Más bien a favor / en contra' -> 'Rather in favor / Rather against'; 'vientre de alquiler' -> 'surrogate womb') -- issues-page line owed at upload. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, 2026-09-22, widened to every CIS survey year 2026-09-23, irw#2381) applied, not re-derived. DESCRIPTION: the IRW dictionary Description ('Being for or against assisted reproduction for an infertile heterosexual couple, a homosexual couple, a single woman, a single man through surrogacy and a woman over 50') names the five P.18 rows; no mismatch. Not confused with sibling _adoption (Bookmark 8, P.17, cols 144-145). No response-data defect.
